claims: The MCP handler registers index_freshness with an empty object schema and delegates to getIndexFreshness(location).
not-indexed applies when the project exists but last_indexed_at is absent; a missing project record instead raises an initialization error.
incomplete takes precedence over stale and covers discovery errors, skipped files, and loss of Git metadata that had previously been recorded.
stale covers file additions, changed hashes, deletions, or a changed/unrecorded Git snapshot.
current requires no incomplete scan, no file differences, and no changed/unrecorded Git snapshot; Git being unavailable alone does not invalidate a non-Git project.
Git report fields include status, indexed/current commit and branch, indexed/current dirty flags, indexed/current changed-path counts, and commitChanged/branchChanged/workingTreeChanged.
A worktree already dirty at indexing time may remain current if its snapshot has not changed.

findings: MCP memory_freshness accepts optional limit 1-500; adapter defaults to 100 and calls getMemoryFreshnessReport.
Report includes eligible non-rejected memories with source_path or commit_sha, sorted by most recently updated and limited; response includes records, total, limit, truncated.
sourceFingerprint stores SHA-256 of source file bytes at memory creation and re-computes it during inspection.
Source statuses: not-linked, unsafe, missing, untracked, current, changed. unsafe/missing/untracked/changed require review; current does not by itself.
Commit statuses: not-referenced, unavailable, unknown, current, ancestor, ahead, diverged. Any status except not-referenced/current requires review.
Either source state or commit relation can make requiresReview true; source current can coexist with commit review requirement.
The operation is read-only and does not mutate memory content, stored fingerprints, or lifecycle state; requiresReview is a report signal.

tasks.task: Trace change_impact from MCP registration through findImpact; explain path normalization, reverse IMPORTS traversal, transitivity, cycle/deduplication handling, limits, truncation, missing target behavior, counters and metadata.

missingTarget.error: File not found in memory index: src/core/not-indexed.ts. Run cnm index.

dotSegments.error: File not found in memory index: src/core/../core/memories.ts. Run cnm index.

findings: Confirmed real change_impact execution, broad reverse-impact result, tight-limit behavior, and missing-index target error.
Located findImpact at src/core/retrieval.ts lines 299-349 and relevant test file metadata.
MCP description indicates recursive reverse importers, but exact traversal semantics were not verified from source body.
Observed that a leading ./ was stripped in the failing path while .. segments were not resolved for that input; agent appropriately limited this inference.
Could not establish exact cycle/deduplication and truncation conditions or full normalization rules because source_excerpt was unavailable and file_details did not expose source bodies.
runs.notes: MCP calls were genuinely executed. Agent obtained useful live graph output and boundary errors, but did not inspect the core implementation body. The unavailable source_excerpt capability is a recurring session-level source-inspection limitation.

findings: MCP registration requires nonempty path; limit is 1-5000 and maxProcessed is 1-10000; defaults are 100 and 1000.
Core path normalization replaces backslashes with forward slashes and strips one leading ./; lookup is exact against indexed files.path; it does not resolve .. segments.
Missing indexed target throws an error recommending cnm index rather than returning an empty result.
Stored IMPORTS edges run from importing source file to imported target file; findImpact traverses them in reverse from target to importers, transitively.
Breadth-first queue plus visited IDs prevents cycles and duplicate affected paths; target itself is initially visited and excluded from affectedFiles.
limit/maxResults caps unique affected files; maxProcessed caps relation rows processed, including rows whose source is already visited.
truncated becomes true when a relation exceeds maxProcessed, a new unvisited affected file is encountered after maxResults is full, or work remains in queue.
processedFiles counts dequeued files including initial target; processedRelations counts relation rows inspected; affectedFiles contains unique importer paths excluding target.
Return shape: file, affectedFiles, truncated, processedFiles, processedRelations, limits.maxResults and limits.maxProcessed.
Tests cover transitive dependents, cycles, duplicate paths, result and processing truncation, invalid limits, and missing target.
